definitions.explanation: The number one when counting things using native Japanese numbers.

examples.japanese: ⟦りんご→りんご：02269_ringo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{一|ひと}つ⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
{一|ひと}つ⟦だけ→だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦{残|のこ}っています→残る：01187_nokoru⟧。
{一|ひと}つ⟦{質問|しつもん}→質問：00888_shitsumon⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧。
⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一|ひと}つ⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
examples.english: The child is one year old.

examples.japanese: {一|ひと}つ⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{残|のこ}っていない→残る：01187_nokoru⟧。
⟦{娘|むすめ}→娘：02263_musume⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{一|ひと}つ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
{一|ひと}つ⟦ずつ→ずつ：03092_zutsu⟧⟦{確認|かくにん}→確認：00158_kakunin⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I'll check them one by one.

examples.japanese: ⟦まだ→まだ：00603_mada⟧{一|ひと}つ⟦なのに→なのに：22395_nanoni⟧⟦{話|はな}せる→話す：00467_hanasu⟧。
examples.english: They can talk even though they're only one.
I have one favor to ask.

examples.japanese: ⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{一|ひと}つ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦ので→ので：09501_node⟧、⟦お→お：03097_o⟧⟦{祝|いわ}い→祝い：01838_iwai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The baby turned one, so we had a celebration.
Our child took their first steps at age one.

notes:
{一|ひと}つ is the native Japanese number 'one,' used for counting general items and as part of many set expressions.

COUNTING PATTERNS:
- {一|ひと}つ, ⟦{二|ふた}つ→二つ：02953_futatsu⟧, ⟦{三|みっ}つ→三つ：02970_mittsu⟧, ⟦{四|よっ}つ→四つ：03039_yottsu⟧, ⟦{五|いつ}つ→五つ：02892_itsutsu⟧
- ⟦{六|むっ}つ→六つ：02974_muttsu⟧, ⟦{七|なな}つ→七つ：02926_nanatsu⟧, ⟦{八|やっ}つ→八つ：02979_yattsu⟧, ⟦{九|ここの}つ→九つ：02902_kokonotsu⟧, ⟦{十|とお}→十：28376_too⟧

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {一|ひと}つ⟦ずつ→ずつ：03092_zutsu⟧: one by one
- {一|ひと}つ⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧ + negative: not even one
- {一|ひと}つ⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧: one level/year above
- {一|ひと}つ⟦お→お：03097_o⟧⟦{願|ねが}い→願い：03529_negai⟧: one request/favor

USAGE:
- This native counting system is used for general items when no specific counter applies, or when the counter is unknown
- Also used informally for age one, as in ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{一|ひと}つ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧ (the child turned one); this native system is used for young children's ages up to about nine
